issues.description: patch_type is "bugfix", but the code style standard (ohos-build-code-style section 12) fixes patch_type to "portability". Semantically the patch is a bugfix, yet the declared project convention is a fixed value; conan-verify / CI did not catch or block it.
issues.fix_suggestion: Set patch_type: "portability" per code style section 12 (or obtain an explicit standard exemption if a bugfix type must be kept).

issues.description: patch_description is a long Chinese prose sentence, while code style section 12 requires space-separated keywords (example: "0001 build aux config.guess").
issues.fix_suggestion: Shorten patch_description to space-separated keywords (e.g. "0001 runlim.c rlimit-as unit") and keep the detailed rationale in notes.md / test-report.md.

issues.description: Cites 'archives/r/runlim/1.10/reports/conan-create.log', which is not part of the change set; *.log is also on the PR forbidden-file list (review rules section 19). No .log file is actually included in the PR.
issues.fix_suggestion: Remove the conan-create.log path citation or point to reports/test-report.md instead; keep the raw log local-only.

summary: Audited the 16-file change set for runlim 1.10 (branch feat/runlim-1.10) against both ohos-build-review-rules and ohos-build-code-style. Independently verified, not merely taken from the archive documents: (1) downloaded https://fmv.jku.at/runlim/runlim-1.10.tar.gz and confirmed its sha256 equals 619aec701e9984977832e2db2bf05cef82ad6ac4ca53b595863bec115b69bc33 as declared in conandata.yml (no fake hash); (2) extracted the pristine tarball and confirmed the R51 inventory claims: the tree contains exactly 7 files (LICENSE NEWS README VERSION configure.sh makefile.in runlim.c), no tests/test/Test anything (find for *test*/*check* returns nothing), makefile.in is 5 lines defining only runlim/clean, configure.sh is 43 lines accepting only -h/--help/-g; (3) dry-ran 'git apply --check -p1' of patches/0001-runlim.c.patch against the pristine runlim.c: it applies cleanly; the hunk @@ -828,21 +828,21 @@ maps to source lines 828-848 and is a single +1/-1 replacement (space_limit -> ((rlim_t) space_limit << 20)) with no __OHOS__ macro and no -D injection (R8 clean); (4) confirmed fix coherence with the real source: defaults are time_limit = real_time_limit = one year and space_limit = get_physical_mb() (MB), and when -t makes time_limit < real_time_limit the code calls setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, space_limit) before execvp, so an unpatched build limits the child to ~space_limit bytes and execvp fails ENOMEM -> EXEC_FAILED rc=1, while the patched value yields rc=2 'out of time'; source status codes (0 ok, 1 execvp failed, 2 out of time, 3 out of memory, 4 SIGSEGV, 11 other signal) and message strings ('usage: runlim', 'invalid option', 'no program specified', 'number argument', 'segmentation fault') match every corresponding test assertion; VERSION comes from makefile.in (-DVERSION="`cat VERSION`") so 'runlim --version' -> 1.10 as asserted; (5) statically counted 32 check/contains call sites in test_package/test_runlim.sh, of which the two 'binary installed' sites are if/else-exclusive, so exactly 31 TAP lines are emitted per run, matching 'echo "1..31"' and MANIFEST.yml assertion_count: 31; passed/failed are accounted and the script exits 1 if any check fails; the test really executes the packaged binary (command -v runlim, real invocations, exit-code and log content assertions) - no empty-shell test (R34) and no skipped or faked pass (R9); (6) all 16 files are LF-only, no BOM, exactly one trailing newline; no TODO/FIXME/XXX or placeholder text in any changed file (PR body and test report clean); no secrets and no absolute Windows paths; no forbidden files (.log/.so/.a/.o/__pycache__/.DS_Store/test-report/SUMMARY.md) included; W2 atomicity holds (one package plus allowed knowledge/drafts); (7) recipe quality: official HTTPS upstream URL plus real sha256 (R39), hardcoded first-adaptation version 1.10 (R37), validate() matches the OHOS family via os in ('Linux','OHOS') (R32), compiler is read from tools.build:compiler_executables rather than a bare shell variable (R33), no system-named shared library so R26 is not applicable, software-level commands.json with type 'tool' and ref 'runlim/1.10' (R38), and manifest status 'built' is truthful (verified but not uploaded; commands.json binary:false). Not independently verifiable in this audit environment: actual OHOS-device execution of the 31 assertions (reports claim 31/31, including CI L1e sabotage verification), the device /proc/<pid>/stat layout probe, and the local patch_generation hashes/absolute paths in manifest.yaml; these claims are internally consistent but rest on the archive reports. Minor observation: MANIFEST.yml describes the local .orig tree as 8 files including the tooling-generated .tarball-sha256, whereas the pristine upstream tarball has 7 - not a mismatch of the R51 conclusions, which were confirmed directly. Findings are advisory only: 3 P3 items (patch_type 'bugfix' vs the code-style-fixed 'portability'; patch_description prose instead of keywords; a dangling conan-create.log citation). There are zero P0/P1: no deception found (R34/R9/R8/R19/R40 clean; R40 needs no platform stub because the only system-level surface, procfs, is claimed device-verified and no fake/return-0 adaptation exists), no L0 structural gate failure, no file:// path, PF7/PF8/PF9 pass, and the R51 inventory/run/truthful-reporting claims match the real upstream tarball. Verdict: pass.
